brief.situation: 13:00 in an outpatient clinic. You are the physical therapist. Mrs. Jensen, 64, was referred by her primary care provider for 'right hip osteoarthritis, strengthening'. She had breast cancer treated 5 years ago and is on hormonal therapy.
handover: No imaging has been done. She has lost weight without trying.

Clinic policy: suspected bone metastasis or impending pathologic fracture: no loading, protected weight bearing on crutches, and a same-day call to the referring provider for imaging and orthopedic referral.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

scoring.modelReasoning: Integrate oncologic history, treatment phase and comorbidities into the movement-system diagnosis. Breast, prostate, lung, kidney and thyroid cancers account for most skeletal metastases, and pain with weight bearing can signal impending pathologic fracture. Mrs. Jensen's femoral, weight-bearing and night pain with weight loss is not hip osteoarthritis: protect the limb, avoid loading, and get same-day imaging and orthopedic referral.
